title: May the itemized statement be emailed to the tenant, or must it be personally delivered or sent by first-class mail?

children.statement: The landlord and tenant mutually agreed, at the start of the tenancy or at any time during or after it, that the statement may be emailed.

source.quote: Upon mutual agreement between the landlord and tenant entered into at the commencement of the tenancy or at any time during or after the tenancy, the itemized statement may be furnished by either of the following:

children.statement: The tenant provided the email account to send it to.

source.quote: Emailed to an account provided by the tenant.

children.statement: The agreement is a separate, optional agreement or is contained in a lease that is itself an electronic record.

source.quote: Except for a separate and optional agreement the primary purpose of which is to authorize a transaction to be conducted by electronic means, an agreement to conduct a transaction by electronic means may not be contained in a standard form contract that is not an electronic record.

children.statement: A clause in a paper form lease is enough mutual agreement to email the statement.

decision.what: Whether to rely on a paper lease clause alone to email the statement, accepting the exposure on the reading that Civil Code 1633.5(b) excludes it.

source.quote: Upon mutual agreement between the landlord and tenant entered into at the commencement of the tenancy or at any time during or after the tenancy, the itemized statement may be furnished by either of the following:

child.statement: More than one adult tenant resides in the unit.

source.quote: if multiple adult tenants reside in the unit, the landlord shall return the remainder of the security by a check made payable to all adult tenants on the rental or lease agreement at the time the tenancy terminates and furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid, to any one of the adult tenants chosen by the landlord.

children.statement: The written agreement with all adult tenants residing in the unit specifies email delivery for each tenant, with the account to use.

source.quote: For each adult tenant, whether the landlord will furnish the itemized statement by email or first-class mail, postage prepaid, along with a forwarding address or email account.

child.statement: For several adult tenants without an all-tenant agreement, the statement must go by personal delivery or first-class mail to one of them, even if a tenant agreed to email.

decision.what: How to deliver the statement for several adult tenants without an all-tenant agreement, accepting the exposure of the other reading.

source.quote: furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid, to any one of the adult tenants chosen by the landlord.

effects.statement: The statement, and with it the photographs by link, may be emailed to the account the tenant provided.

source.quote: Emailed to an account provided by the tenant.

effects.statement: Furnish the statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the address under CA.mailing-address.

source.quote: Subject to subparagraph (C), and except as provided by clause (ii), the landlord shall furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid.

contested.question: Can the mutual agreement to email the statement be a clause in a paper, standard-form lease?

branches.reading: Yes. Subdivision (h)(1)(B)(ii) itself authorizes email on mutual agreement made at the commencement of the tenancy, which is when the lease is signed; the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act limits only the Act's own application.

authority.quote: Upon mutual agreement between the landlord and tenant entered into at the commencement of the tenancy or at any time during or after the tenancy, the itemized statement may be furnished by either of the following:

effect.statement: A paper lease clause supports emailing the statement.

branches.reading: No. An agreement to conduct a transaction electronically may not be contained in a standard-form contract that is not an electronic record, except as a separate and optional agreement, and it may not be inferred from electronic payment. Emailing the statement is conducting the transaction electronically.

authority.quote: Except for a separate and optional agreement the primary purpose of which is to authorize a transaction to be conducted by electronic means, an agreement to conduct a transaction by electronic means may not be contained in a standard form contract that is not an electronic record.

effect.statement: Only a separate, optional agreement (or an electronic lease) supports email; otherwise mail the statement.

contested.question: Where several adult tenants reside and signed no all-tenant agreement, does subparagraph (C)(i)'s personal delivery or first-class mail to one tenant displace an agreement to email the statement?

branches.reading: Yes. Subparagraph (C)(i) governs units with several adult tenants unless all of them sign the clause (ii) agreement, which is where per-tenant email delivery is set.

authority.quote: furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid, to any one of the adult tenants chosen by the landlord.
For each adult tenant, whether the landlord will furnish the itemized statement by email or first-class mail, postage prepaid, along with a forwarding address or email account.

effect.statement: Mail or hand the statement to one adult tenant.

branches.reading: No. Clause (B)(i) is "subject to subparagraph (C)", but the email option in (B)(ii) is not.

authority.quote: Subject to subparagraph (C), and except as provided by clause (ii), the landlord shall furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid.

effect.statement: Email under a mutual agreement remains available.
